title: Another Big Improvement to Another 3 Week Low
summary: Mortgage rates dropped again today, and at a much faster pace than yesterday's decline. Top tier 30yr fixed rates are now down to 7.33% for the average lender, a drop of more than 0.25% from the long-term highs seen just last week. There are a lot of moving parts behind the scenes so let's focus on what we can know or at least reasonably conclude.  [thirtyyearmortgagerates]    Is this the big shift in rates we've been waiting for?  The kind that sometimes follows sustained spikes to long-term highs?   While there's a chance the past 5 days COULD serve as the early indication of a broader rate recovery, it's far too soon to bank on it. The key reason is that much of the paradoxical strength of the past 2 days has been fueled by contagion concerns in the tech space.    What does the tech space have to do with rates? Is it more important than inflation and economic growth?   First off, the tech space and economic growth have a ton of overlap right now. If there's an ongoing pull-back in investor sentiment surrounding AI/tech stocks, and additional concern over certain companies (like Coreweave) having a contagion-like impact on other companies, all of that carries implications for economic data in the future.  The other consideration is AI-related corporate debt. This has been a big driver of upward pressure in rates at times. If investor sentiment is souring on AI-related debt, it decreases the expectations for excess issuance of that debt which, in turn, helps more mainstream rates like Treasuries and mortgages.

title: Exciting Times, But Don't Get Too Excited
summary:
Exciting Times, But Don't Get Too Excited 

             
             
            There's no question that the past 5 days have been the best 5 days that we've seen in a long time in terms of direction movement in rates. They're made all the more miraculous because the past 2 days included much higher inflation readings. In a vacuum, inflation data was bad for rates. But the opposing forces are/were stronger in this case. There are two to consider: AI/tech correction and bond seller exhaustion. We've said for a while that yields would eventually be high enough to prompt some value buying and that 5.34-5.35% may be 2026's version of 2023's 5.00%. As luck would have it, that factor coincided with a rapid increase in the tech sector, primarily driven by Coreweave, but with the word "contagion" also being thrown around. Here's why you should temper excitement: to whatever extent "contagion" doesn't materialize, bonds will lose a good amount of the support they've recently enjoyed. What we've seen so far could be considered "act 1" of a very enjoyable show, but it could also be a short story that ends here. The only surefire justification for a bigger rally is a sustained economic slowdown, preferable coinciding with the war ending and oil falling.

title: What's Up With The Huge Paradoxical Rally?!
summary:
Core PPI was up 0.7 vs 0.3 forecast this morning. That's something that would normally send yields much higher. But everything is different this morning. Bonds rallied sharply in the overnight session and added a bit more to the gains after the 8:30am data. This is on top of yesterday's stunning comeback after getting rocked by higher CPI. To a small extent, the "control group" Retail Sales number may have helped, but the 8:30am gains have more to do with investors waiting to see PPI and finding it would add less than 0.1% to PCE in 2 weeks. This allows the market to maintain its focus on the biggest motivation of the past 2 days: concerns over an AI debt bubble (and big losses in several AI stocks) leading investors to reallocate bond exposure back into Treasuries and portfolio managers to pare equities holdings in favor of bonds. All of the above conveniently coincided with bond yields hitting decades-long highs last week and still being high enough to look like a good buying opportunity today. 
 In the days ahead, it will be useful to keep the historical context in mind. We've seen our fair share of 30bp corrections that have given way to additional selling. For now, this is a sneak preview or a trial balloon for a bigger correction that COULD happen, but isn't necessarily guaranteed. It's what the beginning of such a correction would look like, but things could reverse surprisingly quickly if the market finds a reason to calm down on AI fears.

title: Cash Dominates Home Improvements, Equity Loans Fund Bigger Jobs
summary: A homeowner doesn’t have to be shopping for a new house to face a financing decision. A roof replacement or failed heating system can force one.Cash savings funded 75.7% of home improvement projects in a new LendingTree analysis, far outpacing home equity loans and cash from refinancing. But the projects financed with equity loans were considerably larger, pointing to a different conversation for originators when a repair bill exceeds what a borrower can comfortably pay out of pocket.

title: Mortgage Innovation Depends On The Work We Do Together
summary: A mortgage company can invest in impressive technology and still spend too much time getting information, people, and counterparties to work together.
